rv.q: The touring cast certainly lives up to all the requirements of the piece, from their macho good looks to their inner sensitivity to the quality of their voices.
More than half a century later, “The Outsiders” is a thrilling, can’t-look-away-even-when-you-want-to musical that captures its source material in tone, spirit and story.
This is a stunning and visceral production.
All in all, The Outsiders is an excellent musical and one that can be enjoyed by audiences of all ages.
As I said, this production of THE OUTSIDERS at Shea's is a benchmark musical we’ll be talking about for years.
The production is about as close to perfection as you will likely see.

The Outsiders is a must-see for anyone who grew up loving the novel or film and it’s also a fascinating example of how theatrical technology can evolve while still giving the deep pleasures that only theater brings.

The Outsiders is an authentic American theatrical experience, exposing our societal failures, and holding up the promises of every individual, no matter the side of the tracks where fate led them to be born.
After a night of being transported into 1967. Tulsa, Oklahoma, I can say confidently that I get the hype.
It's both spectacular and intimate at the same time.
The Outsiders is one of the best theatrical productions I’ve seen.
It’s transformative, for the audience as well as the characters — and perhaps for the stage musical world itself.

The movement of the show is muscular with a lot of pop during numbers, and it ascends to another level during the slippery battleground of the rumble, a transfixing sequence choreographed in rain, shadow, light, and slow motion.
This is a show that makes your eyes pop and your heart swell.
The staging was incredible with how deceivingly simple it seems at first.

Most of the changes from page to stage — excising outlying characters, streamlining events, adjusting some plot details — don’t flatten Hinton’s coming-of-age tale but rather sharpen it in Adam Rapp and Justin Levine’s book.
"The Outsiders" crackles on stage the way you remember it doing when you read S. E. Hinton’s 1967 novel in high school.
Solid performances and imaginative staging elevate the production, based on the novel by S.E. Hinton.
My disappointment in the show has to do with the story, not the cast.
Award-winning Broadway touring production boasts athletic choreography and stunning staging, but a weak folk score.

cn.t: Critics praise this Tony-winning musical for its stunning stagecraft, particularly the breathtaking Act II rumble scene in the rain. The production powerfully captures S.E. Hinton's classic story through athletic choreography and visceral theatrical moments.
